title: H2HTalk: Evaluating Large Language Models as Emotional Companion
Architecture of Self-Learning Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The architecture of Self-Learning Artificial Intelligence (SLAI) represents a revolutionary approach to the design of autonomous systems. SLAI integrates cutting-edge technologies such as message-passing neural networks (MPNN), knowledge graphs, and large language models (LLM), creating a unified platform for data analysis, process optimization, and self-directed learning. This system is capable not only of adapting to new conditions but also of efficiently accumulating knowledge, identifying complex dependencies in data, and independently improving its performance. SLAI demonstrates a unique ability to decompose complex tasks, autonomously generate and optimize program code, and uncover hidden patterns. These capabilities enable it to surpass traditional approaches to artificial intelligence, significantly accelerating task execution, reducing errors, and minimizing reliance on human oversight. SLAI lays the foundation for the development of scalable and autonomous systems capable of solving highly complex tasks. Through its ability to integrate, learn, and act, SLAI establishes a cornerstone for the realization of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). However, its development also raises critical questions about the future of human-machine interaction, inviting us to consider a world where systems are not only capable of executing commands but also of making decisions based on their own insights. title: Memorization Capability of Medical Large Language Models and User Privacy Data Disclosure Willingness
abstract: The memorization capability of large language models (LLMs) can enhance the continuity and personalization of services. However, it also gives rise to privacy risks. Grounded in privacy calculus theory, this study investigates how the memorization capability of medical LLMs affects users’ privacy disclosure willingness through two scenario-based experiments. The results indicate that the memorization capability significantly reduces the privacy disclosure willingness. When the memorization capability is enabled, users’ privacy disclosure willingness decreases by 20.9%. This effect is mainly realized through the mediating path of perceived risk. Moreover, the task capability plays a significant moderating role in this relationship. Additional analysis reveals that when the medical LLMs has the memorization capability, the negative relationship between privacy concerns and the privacy disclosure willingness only significant under specific conditions. However, while secrecy in disclosure consistently correlates negatively with disclosure willingness regardless of memorization capability.

title: KI-unterstützter Filmschnitt – Chancen und Herausforderungen
Agentic Edge Intelligence: A Research Agenda
abstract: Agentic AI is rapidly transforming autonomous decision-making, yet its deployment across the edge-cloud continuum remains poorly understood. This paper introduces the concept of agentic edge intelligence, an emerging paradigm in which autonomous agents operate across the computing continuum to negotiate computational resources, data, and services within dynamic digital marketplaces. We position this concept at the intersection of edge intelligence, multi-agent systems, and computational economics, where distributed decision-making replaces centralized orchestration. The paper outlines key research challenges, including scalability, interoperability, market stability, and ethical governance, and proposes a research agenda addressing theoretical, architectural, and societal dimensions. By integrating mechanism design with trustworthy AI and edge computing, the real-time AI economy envisions a self-organizing infrastructure for efficient, transparent, and equitable resource exchange in future digital ecosystems.

title: PRIME Evaluation Framework for Game NPC Dialogue Systems
abstract: 이 연구는 게임 NPC 대화 시스템 평가에서 기존 RAGAS(Retrieval Augmented Generation Assessment) 메트릭의 한계를 실증적으로 입증하고, 인지과학 기반의 PRIME 평가 프레임워크를 제안한다. 4개 RAG 시스템 평가 결과, RAGAS에서 최하위를 기록한 Memory Stream RAG(0.377)가 제안된 PRIME 메트릭 성격 일관성, 관계 발전 추적, 지능 일관성, 기억 감쇠 자연스러움, 감정 일관성에서는 최상위 성능을 보였다. 이는 기존 메트릭이 정확성만을 중시하여 자연스러운 망각과 관계 발전을 오히려 부정적으로 평가하기 때문이다. 이 연구에서 제안한 PRIME 5가지 메트릭은 인간 평가와 r=0.81(p<0.001)의 높은 상관관계를 보여, RAGAS(r=0.23) 대비 3.5배 향상된 타당성을 입증했다. 30명의 숙련된 게이머를 대상으로 한 실험을 통해 제안 프레임워크의 유효성을 검증하였으며, Memory Stream RAG는 NPC 메트릭에서 RAGAS 최하위(4위)에서 최상위(1위)로 3단계 상승하는 결과를 보였다.

title: Research on Multi-node Cooperative Communication Optimization Algorithm for Vehicular Networking
abstract: To address the issues of high communication delay and low throughput in multi-node cooperative communication of vehicular networks (V2X) caused by high dynamic topology and multi-node interference, this paper conducts research on the optimization algorithm for multi-node cooperative communication in vehicular networks, aiming to overcome the shortcomings of existing static optimization algorithms, which have poor adaptability and complex dynamic algorithms. Firstly, it summarizes the multi-node cooperative communication architecture and key technologies of vehicular networks, clarifies the three core issues of dynamic topology, interference suppression, and uneven resource allocation, and constructs a system model and constraints with the goal of "minimizing communication delay + maximizing system throughput". On this basis, a multi-node cooperative optimization algorithm integrating reinforcement learning (DQN) is designed. Through node state perception, collaborative decision generation, resource allocation execution, and performance feedback adjustment, dynamic and efficient cooperation is achieved. A simulation environment is built based on NS-3 and SUMO, and experiments are conducted with greedy algorithm and static resource allocation algorithm as control groups to verify the results. The results show that: in the scenario of vehicle density 20-60 vehicles/km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the communication delay of the proposed algorithm is reduced by 28.3%-35.1% compared with the greedy algorithm, the system throughput is increased by 21.5%-27.8%, the packet delivery rate remains above 96.2%, effectively improving the reliability and real-time performance of multi-node cooperative communication in vehicular networks.

title: Optimal Hovering Control Strategy for UAVs Using PPO
abstract: Hovering stability is a fundamental requirement for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in missions such as surveillance, inspection, and precision delivery. Conventional controllers, such as PID and model-based methods, often face performance degradation under environmental disturbances, sensor noise, and model uncertainties. To address these challenges, this paper presents an optimal hovering control strategy for UAVs using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). A comprehensive state-action representation of UAV dynamics is constructed, and a reward function is designed to jointly encourage precise position holding, energy-efficient control, and disturbance rejection. The proposed policy is trained iteratively in a high-fidelity simulation environment until convergence. To validate its effectiveness, extensive experiments compare the PPO-based controller with two state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning baselines—Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). Results show that the proposed method achieves higher hovering accuracy, improved robustness under wind gusts and sensor noise, and reduced control effort compared with both conventional and DRL baselines. These findings demonstrate the potential of PPO for high-performance autonomous UAV hovering control and provide a solid foundation for real-world deployment and extension to more complex flight tasks.

title: Research on Optimization of Chemical Intelligent Robots Based on Fuzzy PID Controllers
abstract: In order to improve the operation efficiency and accuracy of chemical intelligent robots, a fuzzy PID controller is introduced into the design of the robot's visual system and control system. By optimizing the image processing process and the action process of the mechanical execution end in the chemical scenario, a more stable and efficient chemical operation effect can be achieved. When the visual system processes the images of the chemical operation scenario, it can rely on technical means to screen high-quality images and improve the recognition and matching efficiency of key operation targets (such as chemical equipment components, material containers, etc.). After the target recognition is completed, the fuzzy PID control algorithm is used to accurately control the robot's execution end, enabling it to track the operation targets with higher precision and stably perform the related operation tasks in the chemical field, which provides technical support for the intelligent and automated upgrading of the chemical production process.

title: Research on Path Planning of Path-Finding Robot Based on a GA-ACO Hybrid Algorithm
abstract: To address the problems of long computation time, low efficiency, and poor path quality in the autonomous path planning of path-finding robots in complex environments, a path planning method (GA-ACO) based on the fusion of Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) is proposed. This method leverages GA's strong global search capability to generate high-quality initial path populations and integrates ACO's positive feedback mechanism for local path refinement, forming a "global exploration-local refinement" two-stage collaborative optimization framework. Comparative simulation experiments were conducted in a 100×100 grid environment with 11 mixed rectangular and circular obstacles, using traditional ACO, Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT), and Artificial Potential Field (APF) as comparison algorithms. The simulation results show that the GA-ACO algorithm exhibits significant advantages in key performance indicators: its collision-free success rate reaches 100%, while traditional ACO and RRT achieve 0%; the average path length is 118.46 units, which is 58.8% shorter than traditional ACO (287.54 units), 79.8% shorter than RRT (585.40 units), and 78.6% shorter than APF (553.82 units); the safety margin is 0.68 units, 33 times higher than APF's 0.02 units. Although its computation time (4.35s) is slightly longer than the contrast algorithms (0.2-0.3s), this minimal cost is fully compensated by the substantial improvements in path quality and safety. The proposed algorithm provides a reliable technical solution for path planning of path-finding robots in complex static obstacle environments.

title: Research on the Artificial Intelligence Distribution Strategy for Facility Configuration Based on the Ant Colony Algorithm
abstract: This paper uses a computational approach to apply the ant colony algorithm to community sports facility configuration. A matching model is built via programming after data-driven analysis of facility development and in-depth study of the algorithm's principles. It turns real-world problems into a computational framework. The algorithm is integrated into the configuration design. Programming optimizes the design for resource allocation. Combining the multi-objective function model with computational requirements, optimal solution sets for different objectives are generated. Code programming combines the objective function and the algorithm, updating the function value continuously. Iterative computations yield a stable optimal solution, offering an advanced computational method for facility configuration. Simulation experiments show the proposed algorithm outperforms traditional ones in reliability and stability. It generates diverse solutions, enabling more efficient computational matching and utilization. This research presents a new computational paradigm for intelligent facility configuration.

title: Study on Scheduling and Path Optimization of Warehouse Logistics Mobile Robots in Supply Chain Task Allocation and Warehouse Logistics Control Systems
abstract: To address the problems in supply chain task allocation and warehouse logistics control systems where the scheduling system struggles to allocate tasks quickly and accurately, and the handling routes are not the shortest or optimal when mobile robots execute order tasks, a reconfigurable warehouse space model and grid map model are constructed based on the movement mode of mobile robots and order task requirements. For the supply chain task allocation scenario, a mathematical model is established to solve the problem of minimizing the total completion time of order tasks; in response to the needs of warehouse logistics control systems, the shortcomings of three commonly used distance algorithms in the traditional A* algorithm are improved, and a complex diagonal distance algorithm is proposed for path planning simulation. The simulation results show that the above methods achieve the shortest total task completion time in supply chain task allocation, and reduce the number of search nodes by 30% and the path length by 20% in path planning within warehouse logistics control systems.

title: Real-Time Feature Extraction of Interactive Information for the Digital Economy: Design and Application of Artificial Intelligence Deep Learning Models
abstract: In the context of the digital economy, interactive information exhibits characteristics of high dimensionality, significant nonlinear relationships, and urgent real-time processing requirements, due to its wide range of sources, diverse collection devices, high sampling frequency, and strong coupling among variables. Traditional feature extraction methods not only struggle to adapt to the nonlinear characteristics of interactive information (leading to reduced accuracy in subsequent data mining) but also fail to meet the real-time requirements of the digital economy in terms of processing efficiency. To address this issue, this paper focuses on the design and application of artificial intelligence deep learning models and proposes a Mutual Information-based Real-time Feature Extraction (MIFE) algorithm: improved mutual information is used as the evaluation criterion for feature extraction, and the advantage of deep learning models in fitting nonlinear data is leveraged to enhance the accuracy of subsequent interactive information mining; meanwhile, an adaptive sliding window technology is introduced to realize real-time processing of incremental interactive information at a low computational cost. By integrating historical data and dynamically added new data, rapid dimensionality reduction of the entire interactive information dataset is achieved. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm (combined with the application of deep learning models) can efficiently complete the feature extraction of interactive information and demonstrates excellent accuracy in verification with multiple classifiers, providing technical support for the real-time analysis of interactive information in digital economy scenarios.

title: Design of Real-Time SLAM Algorithm for Quadruped Robots in Complex Terrains
abstract: To address the poor adaptability of traditional SLAM algorithms to quadruped robots in complex terrains, this study optimizes the collaboration between real-time SLAM and quadruped robots. ORB-SLAM2 is improved by adding a dense mapping thread: combined with a Kinect camera and filtering, a dense point cloud is built, and a 3D semantic map is generated by fusing YOLO v5 and super-voxel clustering. Hector-SLAM is optimized using bicubic interpolation to enhance grid map accuracy, and EKF to fuse IMU and odometer data for motion distortion correction and map ghosting elimination, with effectiveness verified via AGV navigation experiments. An exploratory gait for the quadruped robot is designed for obstacle avoidance through tactile sensing; PSO optimizes step length, height, and cycle, with joint kinematic limits as constraints, balancing speed, stability, and other indicators. Results show the improved SLAM provides high-precision perception, and the optimized gait enhances complex terrain adaptability, supporting quadruped robot applications.

title: Motivating Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder to Talk with an Conversational Android Robot System Changing Context Awareness
abstract: Android robot applications for individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) to help learn social communication skills are widely investigated. To provide individuals with ASD with more opportunities and maintain motivation for regularly talking with android robots, these androids need to allow individuals to talk about anything at any time. This study introduces an autonomous open-domain dialogue android robot system to conversations with individuals with ASD, to investigate its potential to motivate them to talk. We employ the android robot system that is capable of generating two types of utterances, context-aware and context-free, and conduct a conversational experiment. Each participant talks with our robot system and assesses the impressions and preference for different types of robot utterances. The experimental results indicate that preferences for context awareness in robot utterances differ among ASD participants, and with their preferred system, each participant has a significantly higher motivation to have further conversations.

title: Co-MAS: Towards Robust Multi-Agentic AI Assistant through Multi-Layered Reflection
abstract: AI Agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit outstanding promise in tasks that call for cognitive abilities comparable to those of humans. But they usually have trouble solving complicated analytical data science problems that require multi-step, structured reasoning. We introduce Copilot Multi-Agentic System (Co-MAS), a system with multiple agents designed to handle complex analytical and reasoning tasks by using Finite State Machine (FSM) interactions. Co-MAS consists of a Planner Agent, Analyzer Agent, Validator Agent, Executer Agent, and Presenter Agent. Since these agents are horizontal in nature, Co-MAS can effectively address complex analytical and data science problems in any domain with a relevant context. With an average 12% increase in accuracy, Co-MAS significantly boosts standalone LLM performance in analytics and data science tasks. It accomplishes over 90% accuracy in a variety of machine learning tasks and an astounding 95.55% accuracy on the InfiAgent DA-bench dataset. Additionally, our solution maintains an average accuracy of 88% across top enterprise LLMs, demonstrating its LLM-agnostic nature.

title: Sari Sandbox: A Virtual Retail Store Environment for Embodied AI Agents
abstract: We present Sari Sandbox, a high-fidelity, photorealistic 3D retail store simulation for benchmarking embodied agents against human performance in shopping tasks. Addressing a gap in retail-specific sim environments for embodied agent training, Sari Sandbox features over 250 interactive grocery items across three store configurations, controlled via an API. It supports both virtual reality (VR) for human interaction and a vision language model (VLM)-powered embodied agent. We also introduce SariBench, a dataset of annotated human demonstrations across varied task difficulties. Our sandbox enables embodied agents to navigate, inspect, and manipulate retail items, providing baselines against human performance. We conclude with benchmarks, performance analysis, and recommendations for enhancing realism and scalability. The source code can be accessed via https://github.com/upeee/sari-sandbox-env.

title: Security Risks and Privacy Challenges of Large Language Models in Enterprise Environments
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are increasingly adopted across sectors including education, healthcare, and corporate environments. While they offer operational efficiencies, their integration raises significant data security and compliance concerns. This study evaluates whether LLMs retain and disclose sensitive organizational data when exposed to proprietary inputs such as HR records, financial documents, and code samples. Using controlled experiments, we assessed the susceptibility of these models to prompt injection and role-based manipulation attacks. Findings indicate that both models exhibit varying degrees of data leakage and compliance violations, particularly in the context of GDPR and intellectual property protections. Based on these results, we propose a practical framework to guide the responsible use of LLMs in enterprise environments. The framework includes mitigation strategies for minimizing data exposure, ensuring regulatory compliance, and reducing the risks associated with AI integration in the workplace.

title: Exploratory models of human-AI teams
abstract: Abstract As human-agent teaming (HAT) research continues to grow, computational methods for modeling HAT behaviors and measuring HAT effectiveness also continue to develop. One rising method involves the use of human digital twins (HDT) to approximate human behaviors and socio-emotional-cognitive reactions to AI-driven agent team members. To help HDT research effectively model human trust in HATs, we offer two lines of insight. First, through a review of the HAT trust literature, we identify key characteristics and attributes of trust that must be considered in order to properly conceptualize, model, and measure trust. Through this review, we outline the theoretical foundations of trust needed for effective HDTs capable of emulating human trust and offer guidance on where and how extant HAT research should translate into HDT modeling and future research. Second, through causal analyses of archival team communication data from a HAT experiment, we supplement theoretical foundations for modeling trust with data-driven insights to guide the trust-related language HDTs may need to effectively emulate human trust. Finally, we discuss implications of these combined theoretical and empirical insights for future HDT research, highlighting the necessity of ongoing validation against human behaviors and the refinement of computational methods. This paper ultimately aims to advance both the fidelity and applicability of HDTs in modeling nuanced human-agent trust dynamics, fostering more effective and realistic human-agent collaborations.

title: Survey of Agents Methodologies in the Financial Domain
Research on End-to-End SLAM Framework Based on Deep Feature Learning
abstract: To address the issues of traditional simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) that rely on manual features, poor robustness in dynamic scenarios, and complex multimodule coupling, this paper proposes an end-to-end SLAM framework based on deep feature learning. This framework consists of four major modules: the input layer, the multi-scale deep feature extraction layer, the joint estimation layer of pose and semantic map, and the loop closure detection optimization layer. The multi-scale deep feature extraction layer uses an improved ResNet combined with an attention mechanism to enhance the discrimination of key region features. The joint estimation layer of pose and semantic map filters dynamic objects through semantic segmentation to improve map robustness. The loop closure detection optimization layer achieves global consistency correction based on deep feature matching. Experiments on the TUM RGB-D and KITTI Odometry datasets show that the absolute trajectory error (ATE) of this framework in static scenarios is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1 8. 2 \%}$</tex> lower than that of ORB-SLAM3. In dynamic scenarios, the map integrity reaches 89.7 % (an increase of 12.5 % compared to DF-SLAM), and the real-time frame rate remains above 25 FPS, which can meet the real-time high-precision requirements of scenarios such as autonomous driving and service robots, effectively breaking through the performance bottleneck of traditional SLAM in complex scenarios.

title: Study on Financial Credit Default Risk Prediction Method Based on the Optuna-Lp-SVM Model
abstract: Aiming at the problems of large data volume, high dimensionality, unbalanced samples and significant noise interference in financial credit default data, this paper proposes and studies a financial credit default risk prediction method based on the Optuna-Lp-SVM model. Based on the support vector machine, the model assigns differentiated weights to different prediction errors through a cost matrix and combines multi-kernel learning to construct a hybrid kernel function combination. It uses the Optuna framework to realize automatic tuning of misclassification costs, kernel function parameters and weights, and introduces Lp norm constraint on kernel function weights to enhance the model's robustness to noise and abnormal data. In the experiment, the Optuna-Lp-SVM models with 4 commonly used basic kernel function combinations were verified and compared with single-kernel support vector machine, K-nearest neighbor, logistic regression and Gaussian Naive Bayes algorithms. The results show that on the financial credit default dataset, the g-mean and AUC indicators of the Optuna-Lp-SVM model are better than those of the comparison algorithms, and it still maintains good performance on datasets with different variances of noise added, which can be effectively applied to financial credit default risk prediction.

title: Research on a Large Model for Children's Multimodal Emotion Recognition Based on Multi-Feature Cross-Fusion
abstract: To accurately identify children's emotional tendencies in multimodal data from daily and educational scenarios (supporting psychological needs understanding, educational strategy optimization, and mental health interventions), this study proposes a multi-feature cross-fusion-based children's multimodal emotion recognition model (BCVAFC) to solve existing issues of fragmented feature extraction and insufficient inter-modal fusion. The model enhances features by introducing CLIP alongside BERT (text) and ViT (image), mapping text (e.g., speech-to-text) and image (e.g., facial frames) to a shared semantic space via contrastive learning; it then captures inter-modal dependencies through a text-image dual-guided cross-attention mechanism fused with self-attention and Fourier convolution, and achieves deep fusion of low-level and high-level features via global attention and residual connections to boost recognition accuracy. Experiments on children's emotion datasets show BCVAFC outperforms traditional multimodal models in recognizing emotions like joy, anxiety, and grievance, with accuracy converging stably to 92.3% and good robustness; adapted to children's data characteristics, it can be expanded with more modalities (e.g., body movements, heart rate) for wider applications.

title: Enabling Large Language Models and Agentic Workflows on Legacy GPU Architectures for Building Scalable Farmer Advisory Systems in India
Thought flow nets: From single predictions to trains of model thought
abstract: Abstract When humans solve complex problems, they typically construct, reflect, and revise sequences of ideas, hypotheses, and beliefs until a final decision or conclusion is reached. Contrary to this, current machine learning models are mostly trained to map an input to one single and fixed output. In this paper, we investigate how we can equip models with the ability to represent, construct, and evaluate a second, third, and $k$ -th thought within their prediction process. Drawing inspiration from Hegel’s dialectics, we propose and evaluate the thought flow concept which constructs a sequence of predictions. We present a self-correction mechanism which (a) is trained to estimate the model’s correctness and which (b) performs iterative prediction updates based on the gradient of the correctness prediction. We introduce our method focusing initially on question answering (QA) and carry out extensive experiments which demonstrate that (i) our method is able to correct its own predictions and that (ii) it can improve model performance by a large margin. In addition, we conduct a qualitative analysis of thought flow correction patterns and explore how thought flow predictions affect users’ human-AI collaboration in a crowdsourcing study. We find that (iii) thought flows improve user performance and are perceived as more natural, correct, and intelligent regarding single and/or top-3 predictions.
